articles.title: Understand how accounting works in MESAPAY
articles.summary: What's in the Accounting and Reports menus, how MESAPAY builds one summary entry per month and per source from your operation, and how entries for open months keep themselves up to date.
articles.body:
MESAPAY accounting turns what happens in your restaurant (sales, payments, purchases, expenses, payroll) into double-entry entries on the Colombian chart of accounts (PUC). That way you and your accountant get books, financial statements and taxes without keying in every sale.

> If you don't see **Accounting** or **Reports** in the side menu, your business doesn't have the accounting module turned on. Contact support if you need it.

## Who can see it

The accounting screens are available to users with the Operator role. If your accountant is going to work directly in MESAPAY, create a user for them in [Settings › Users](/operator/settings/usuarios), as explained in [Create your team's users](/operator/ayuda/primeros-pasos/usuarios-y-roles).

## The two menus

**Accounting** holds the month's work: **Expenses & journal** (the Accounting screen and its tabs), **Chart of accounts**, **Vouchers**, **General ledger**, **General journal / auxiliary**, **Budgets**, **Fixed assets**, **Deferrals** and **Period close**.

**Reports** holds what you look up, export and print: **All reports**, **Sales commissions**, **Receivables & payables**, **Period taxes**, **Statement of financial position**, **Income statement**, **Trial balance** and **Third-party information (exógena)**.

[All reports](/operator/reportes) shows each report as a card, grouped into **Accounting**, **Financial**, **Tax**, **Commercial** and **Operational**. Operational includes the **Shift close-out**, the **Operating P&L** and the **Sales and purchase books**.

## The Accounting tabs

- **Expenses**: rent, utilities and other business expenses. See [Record expenses and recurring expenses](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/registrar-gastos).
- **P&L** and **Books**: the month's result and the sales and purchase books. See [Read the monthly P&L and export the books](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/pyg-y-libros-del-mes).
- **Chart of accounts**: see [Adjust the chart of accounts](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/plan-de-cuentas).
- **Journal**: the month's entries, when they were last updated, and the buttons to refresh them now and close the month. See [Generate the entries and close the month](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/cerrar-el-mes-contable).
- **Statements**: a summary of the income statement, the statement of financial position and the trial balance for the month, marked **Balanced** or **Not balanced**.
- **Taxes**, **Banks**, **Assets** and **Budget**: see [taxes and withholdings](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/impuestos-y-retenciones), [bank reconciliation](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/conciliacion-bancaria), [fixed assets and deferrals](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/activos-fijos-y-diferidos) and [budgets and cost centers](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/presupuestos-y-centros-de-costos).

At the top is the month picker (◀ ▶). Every tab shows the selected month, except **Chart of accounts**, **Banks** and **Assets**, which don't depend on the month.

## How the entries are built

MESAPAY doesn't post one entry per sale. For each month it builds **one summary entry per source**, dated the last day of the month:

- **Sales for the month**: what was collected, split by payment method (cash goes to the cash account, your own card reader to banks, online payments to the gateway balance and credit sales to customers), against revenue, the VAT or INC each invoice locked in, and tips payable.
- **Customer payments**, **Supplier payments** and **Expense payments**.
- **Purchases for the month**: the purchase orders received, with their deductible VAT and withholdings, against suppliers.
- **Cost of goods sold** and **Waste**, if you use inventory and recipes.
- **Expenses for the month**, **Payroll**, **Monthly depreciation**, **Deferral amortization**, **Refunds** and **Credit notes for the month**.

On top of those come the ones you record yourself: manual vouchers, bank movements, tax payments and the year-end closing.

## Entries update on their own

Every day at 5:30 a.m., MESAPAY rebuilds the summary entries for the open months, from the first month with activity through the current month, with whatever is there at that moment. A sale, a purchase received or an expense recorded today reaches the books the next morning, without you doing anything.

- Closed months are left untouched: their vouchers are already numbered and final.
- Your manual vouchers are left untouched too.
- The **Journal** tab shows when the month's entries were last updated.

If you need the books up to date before the next update:

1. Go to [Accounting](/operator/contabilidad?tab=diario) and open the **Journal** tab.
2. Pick the month with ◀ ▶.
3. Tap **Generate / refresh entries**.

The general journal, the general ledger, the trial balance and the financial statements read those entries. The **P&L** and the sales and purchase **Books**, on the other hand, are calculated live from the operation and don't wait for the update.

## Common cases

- **The general ledger or the income statement is empty**: that month's entries haven't been built yet; it happens, for example, on the first day of the month before 5:30 a.m. Go to the **Journal** tab and tap **Generate / refresh entries**.
- **I recorded an expense and it doesn't show in the books**: it comes in with the next morning's update. If you need it now, tap **Generate / refresh entries** in the expense's month. If that month is already closed, reopen it first.
- **"The entries are being updated right now. Try again in a minute."**: the automatic update (or someone else) is building your business's entries. Wait a minute and tap the button again.
- **The P&L and the income statement don't match**: that's expected. The P&L is an operating summary; the income statement comes from the entries, with revenue net of tax and after credit notes, refunds, depreciation and manual vouchers.
- **A summary entry is missing after generating**: this happens if you deactivated every sub-account under an account MESAPAY posts to (for example, Banks). Activate at least one in the chart of accounts and generate again.

articles.title: Record expenses and recurring expenses
articles.summary: Record rent, utilities, fees and other expenses with their account, supplier and cost center, say whether you already paid them and schedule the ones that repeat every month.
articles.body:
Expenses are what the restaurant pays for that isn't a supply purchase: rent, utilities, internet, professional fees, advertising, maintenance. Once you record them, the P&L deducts them and they go into the month's accounting.

> Supply purchases from suppliers are recorded in **Back office › Purchasing** (if you have that module), not here.

## Record an expense

1. Go to [Accounting › Expenses & journal](/operator/contabilidad). The **Expenses** tab opens on the current month, with the **Month total**.
2. Tap **New expense**.
3. Fill in the details (each one is explained below).
4. If you already paid it, leave **Already paid** checked and choose under **Paid from** the cash or bank account the money came out of. If you still owe it, uncheck it and enter the date under **Due**.
5. Tap **Save**.

The expense details:

- **Category** (required): type it freely, for example "Rent" or "Utilities". The ones you've used before show up as suggestions.
- **Description**: optional.
- **Amount** and **Date** (required). The date decides which month the expense falls in.
- **Supplier**: if you have the purchasing module, pick one or create it right there with **+ New supplier**.
- **Cost center**: shows up once you've created cost centers. See [Build budgets and use cost centers](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/presupuestos-y-centros-de-costos).
- **Expense account**: the PUC account it's charged to. With **Automatic (from the category)**, MESAPAY works it out from the words in the category (in Spanish): rent, fees, internet or phone, utilities, maintenance, commissions, advertising or payroll. Anything it doesn't recognize goes to miscellaneous expenses. If your accountant opened their own accounts, it's better to pick one.

## Recurring expenses

For expenses that repeat the same every month, like rent or the internet plan:

1. Tap **New expense** and fill in the category, amount and other details.
2. Turn on **Recurring expense (repeats every month)**.
3. Under **Day of the month (1-28)**, enter the day it should be created.
4. Tap **Save**.

The template stays in the **Recurring expenses** list, marked **Recurring** with the text "Every month on day…". On that day, MESAPAY creates the month's expense on its own, with the template's category, description, amount, supplier, expense account and cost center. If it couldn't be created that day, it comes out as soon as possible within the same month, dated on the chosen day. That expense is left as pending payment.

> If you create the template after the chosen day, the first expense comes out next month. Record this month's by hand.

To stop repeating it, open the template and tap **Remove**. Expenses already created in previous months are kept.

## Edit or delete an expense

1. Pick the month with ◀ ▶ and tap the expense in the list.
2. Change what you need and tap **Save**, or tap **Remove** and confirm.

Editing doesn't change what was already recorded as paid.

## What happens in the accounting

When you generate the month's entries, expenses go into the **Expenses for the month** entry: debit to each expense's account and credit to costs and expenses payable. What you marked as paid goes into **Expense payments**: debit to costs and expenses payable and credit to the cash or bank account you chose. Expenses still owed show up in [Receivables & payables › payables](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/cartera), with their due date.

## Common cases

- **"Check the fields: some values are invalid."**: the category or the date is missing.
- **"Invalid amount."**: the amount has to be greater than zero.
- **"Pick the day of the month (1-28) for the recurring expense."**: enter a day between 1 and 28.
- **"A supplier with that name already exists."**: pick it from the list instead of creating it again.
- **I don't see the Supplier field**: it depends on the purchasing module. Contact support if you need it.
- **I left it as owed and have now paid it**: in the list, expenses still owed show **To pay** and the balance. Tap the expense and, under **Record payment**, enter the **Amount paid** (it can be a partial payment), the **Payment date** and, under **Paid from**, the cash or bank account. Tap **Record payment**. The payment goes into the **Expense payments** entry for the month of the payment date; once the balance reaches zero, the expense says **Paid on…** and leaves the payables.
- **I recorded an expense in a month that's already closed**: it shows in **Expenses** and in the P&L, but it doesn't reach the books until you reopen that month and generate the entries again. See [Generate the entries and close the month](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/cerrar-el-mes-contable).

articles.title: Read the monthly P&L and export the books
articles.summary: The P&L sums up the month's sales, costs, expenses and profit live from your operation. The Books tab lists sales and purchases, and that's where the CSV files and the Excel for your accountant come from.
articles.body:
The **P&L** tells you at a glance whether the month is turning a profit, and **Books** gives you the sales and purchase detail to hand to your accountant. Both tabs are calculated live from what happens in the restaurant: no need to generate entries.

## See the month's P&L

1. Go to [Accounting › P&L](/operator/contabilidad?tab=pnl).
2. Pick the month with ◀ ▶.

It reads from top to bottom:

- **Sales revenue**: what you collected in the month excluding tax and tips, net of discounts and minus credit notes and refunds. Below it you see where it comes from: **Sales at menu price**, minus **Discounts**, **Tax included in the price (INC/VAT)**, **Credit notes for the month** and **Refunds without a credit note** (deductions at zero are hidden). For reference only, **Tips (informational)** and, if you charged off-menu items with tax on top, **Tax added on top of off-menu charges (informational)**.
- **COGS (actual consumption)**: the cost of the supplies that left inventory according to the recipes of what was sold.
- **Waste**: what was written off from inventory.
- **Gross profit**, with its percentage of sales.
- **Labor cost**: if you have the schedules module, the base salaries plus the holiday and Sunday surcharges from the shifts.
- **Expenses**: by category, including **Non-inventory supply purchases**.
- **Operating profit**: green when there's a profit and red when there's a loss.

Further down:

- **Taxes**: **Sales tax** with its **Taxable base**, by rate, already net of the month's credit notes and refunds (if something was deducted, under the rate you see the **Gross tax** and each deduction), and **Taxes on purchases** (VAT, INC and withholdings). To change the sales tax tap **Configure**, which takes you to Settings › Taxes. See [Set up the sales tax](/operator/ayuda/facturacion/impuesto-de-ventas).
- **Sales by category**: sales excluding tax and net of discounts, COGS and margin for each menu category. Credit notes and refunds aren't split by category.
- **Prime cost (COGS + waste + labor)**: the share of sales that goes to supplies and staff (with the schedules module).
- **Purchases received this month (informational)**: what came in from suppliers. It doesn't reduce the result: the cost comes in through COGS when it's consumed.

## See the sales and purchase books

1. Go to [Accounting › Books](/operator/contabilidad?tab=books) and pick the month.
2. Choose **Sales** or **Purchases**.

**Sales** lists every bill collected in the month: table or pickup, tip, tax, total and invoice number, with totals **By payment method**. If you issue electronic credit notes, they show under **Credit notes for the month**: the ones accepted by the DIAN and dated in the month, which reduce sales, plus the **Total net of credit notes**. See [Issue an electronic credit note](/operator/ayuda/facturacion/notas-credito).

**Purchases** lists the purchase orders received in the month, with supplier, invoice number and due date, marked **Paid**, **To pay** or **Overdue**, and the totals **Received this month** and **Total to pay**.

## Export for your accountant

In the **Books** tab:

- **Export CSV**: the book you have open (sales or purchases) for the month.
- **Export expenses (CSV)**: the month's expenses.
- **Download Excel for the accountant**: a single file with the Sales, Withholdings, Cost of sales and Inventory sheets. In Sales, the month's accepted credit notes appear as negatives and the total is net of them.

> Amounts come as numbers, so your accountant can add them up and filter them.

> To see sales by day, hour, dish or waiter and compare them with another period, use [Analyze your sales](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/analizar-las-ventas).

## Common cases

- **COGS shows zero**: if you see "No consumption recorded this month yet…", COGS needs the inventory and recipes modules, and the dishes need recipes. Purchases are never used as cost.
- **"This business is invoicing WITHOUT sales tax."**: review the tax with your accountant in Settings › Taxes.
- **The P&L doesn't match the income statement**: the P&L is an operating summary; it doesn't include depreciation, deferrals or manual vouchers, and it counts each credit note in the month of its issue date (in the entries, a note from an already closed month goes into the first open month). For accounting figures use the income statement, which comes from the entries. See [View the official books and financial statements](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/libros-y-estados-financieros).
- **Labor cost doesn't show up**: it depends on the schedules module and on your team having salaries. If you see "employees without a salary", fill them in under Schedules.
- **An expense doesn't change the profit**: check its date; it counts in that date's month.

articles.title: Adjust the chart of accounts
articles.summary: MESAPAY ships the PUC for restaurants under IFRS for SMEs. Create accounts and sub-accounts (with AI help if you like), import your accountant's chart, export it and deactivate the accounts you don't use.
articles.body:
The chart of accounts is the list of PUC accounts where every entry lands. MESAPAY ships it ready for restaurants, under IFRS for SMEs (Group 2), and you or your accountant can adapt it: create accounts and sub-accounts, import the accountant's chart, export it and deactivate what you don't use.

## Find an account

1. Go to [Accounting › Chart of accounts](/operator/contabilidad?tab=chart).
2. Type a code or a name in **Search by code or name…**.

Accounts are shown as a tree: class (1 digit), group (2), account (4), sub-account (6) and auxiliaries (8 and 10). Each one shows its type and its nature (**Debit** or **Credit**). Grouping accounts don't take entries; entries land in their child accounts.

## Create an account or a sub-account

1. Tap **New account**, or **Add sub-account** next to the account that will be the parent.
2. Under **Parent account**, search for it by code or name and select it. The new account inherits its type and nature.
3. Under **Code**, enter the parent's code plus two digits. For example, under 111005 goes 11100501.
4. Enter the **Name**, for example "Bancolombia savings".
5. Tap **Create account**.

### With help from AI

In the same form, under **Suggest with AI**, describe the account you need (for example, "Bancolombia savings account" or "tips payable") and tap **Suggest with AI**. The AI fills in the parent, the code and the name, and explains why it chose that spot. Review it and fix anything needed: nothing is created until you tap **Create account**.

### If the parent already had entries

When you create a sub-account under an account that was already receiving entries, MESAPAY moves them to the new sub-account and the parent becomes a grouping account. You'll see the message "Account … created. Parent … had entries: … lines were moved to the new sub-account." The balance isn't lost: it now lives in the sub-account.

From then on, whatever MESAPAY posted to the parent lands in the sub-account. If you open several sub-accounts under an account MESAPAY uses (for example, one per bank), automatic entries go to the one ending in 05 or, if there isn't one, to the lowest code.

## Import your accountant's chart

1. Tap **Import my accountant's chart of accounts**.
2. Paste the accounts, one per line: code, name, nature and whether it accepts entries. For example, `110505;Caja general;D;true`.
3. Tap **Import accounts**.

You can copy the columns straight from a spreadsheet: semicolons, tabs or commas all work, and the first row can hold the column titles. Nature takes D or C; accepts entries takes "true", "sí", "S", "X" or "1" (blank leaves it as a grouping account).

Importing only adds: it creates the new accounts, updates the name and nature of existing ones and creates any missing grouping accounts. It never deletes. At the end you see how many were created and updated and, if any, the lines that were left out with the reason.

## Export

**Export CSV** downloads the whole chart: code, name, type, nature, whether it takes entries and whether it's active.

## Rename or deactivate

1. Tap **Edit** next to the account.
2. Change the name and tap **Save**, or tap **Deactivate** (or **Activate**).

No account is ever deleted. Deactivated ones are marked **Inactive**.

## Common cases

- **"Can't deactivate: the account has entries."**: an account with entries can't be deactivated.
- **"Can't deactivate: the accounting engine posts to this account."**: it's one of the accounts MESAPAY uses for automatic entries (cash, banks, sales, VAT, suppliers…). If you want more detail, create sub-accounts under it.
- **"Can't deactivate: it has active child accounts."**: deactivate the children first.
- **"Activate the parent account first."**: activate the parent and then the child.
- **"The code must start with the parent's code and have exactly two more digits."**: check the code.
- **"An account with that code already exists."**: use another code or find the existing one.
- **"AI isn't available right now."**: create the account by hand or try again later.
- **"No valid account was found in what you pasted."**: check that each line starts with a numeric code of 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 or 10 digits, with the class between 1 and 6.

articles.title: Generate the entries and close the month
articles.summary: Generate the month's entries, check that they balance and close the period: the vouchers are numbered and locked. When the year ends, generate the year-end closing entry.
articles.body:
Closing the month makes the books final: the vouchers up to that month get consecutive numbers and the period is locked, so nothing changes after your accountant has reviewed it. At the end of the year, you also generate the year-end closing entry.

## Before closing

1. Check that everything for the month is in: purchases received, expenses, payroll, bank reconciliation and manual vouchers.
2. Go to [Accounting › Journal](/operator/contabilidad?tab=diario), pick the month with ◀ ▶ and tap **Generate / refresh entries**.
3. Open the **Statements** tab and check that the statement of financial position and the trial balance say **Balanced**.
4. Create a backup, in case you need to go back. See [Create and restore backups](/operator/ayuda/impresion-y-equipos/copias-de-seguridad).

## Close the month

1. Go to [Accounting › Period close](/operator/contabilidad/cierre).
2. Under **Closing status** you see the **Last month closed** and the **Next voucher number**.
3. In the **Months of** (year) table, each month shows as **Closed**, **Open** or **Future**, with how many vouchers it has and how many are already numbered. Switch years with ◀ ▶.
4. Tap **Close month** on the month's row and confirm.

Months close in order: the button only appears on the month after the last one closed (or, if you've never closed, on the first month with vouchers), and never on a future month. The **Journal** tab also has **Close month**: closing a month there also closes any earlier months that are still open.

### What happens when you close

- Unnumbered vouchers up to that month, including those from earlier months, get consecutive numbers in date order. In open months, entries show as unnumbered.
- The month is locked: its entries can no longer be regenerated and no vouchers can be recorded with a date in that month. In **Journal** you'll see "Period closed through…".
- An expense you record with a date in a closed month shows in **Expenses** and in the P&L, but doesn't reach the books while the month stays closed.
- An accepted electronic credit note dated in a closed month is accounted for in the first open month.

## Reopen the last month

If something needs fixing:

1. Under **Closing status**, tap **Reopen last month** (with the month's name) and confirm. It's also in the **Journal** tab.
2. The lock moves back one month. Make the fix and tap **Generate / refresh entries** again.
3. Close the month again.

Numbers already assigned are kept. If you regenerated, the new entries get new numbers when you close again, continuing the sequence. Only the last closed month can be reopened: to reach an earlier one, reopen them one at a time.

> While the reopened month still has numbered automatic entries, the automatic morning update doesn't regenerate it, so that numbering doesn't change without your say. That's why, after making the fix, you tap **Generate / refresh entries** in that month.

## Year-end closing

When the year ends:

1. Close all twelve months. While any is missing, the section tells you how many are still open.
2. Under **Year-end closing** (the year), tap **Generate closing entry** and confirm.

A single entry dated December 31 is created that closes the income statement accounts (classes 4, 5 and 6) and takes the net to 360505 (profit for the year) or 361005 (loss for the year). The section shows the date it was generated and the **Profit for the year** or **Loss for the year**. If you change something afterwards, tap **Regenerate closing entry**: it updates the entry with the current balances and, if it already has a voucher number, keeps that number. A numbered voucher is never deleted: with December closed, a numbered closing can only be regenerated if the balances haven't changed.

## Common cases

- **"There are no vouchers yet: generate the month's journal before closing."**: go to **Journal** and tap **Generate / refresh entries**.
- **Close month doesn't show on the month I want**: an earlier month still needs closing. If you see "The next month to close is…", tap **View** (the year) to go to it.
- **"That month is already closed. Reload the page."**: someone closed it from another screen. Reload the page.
- **"There is no closed month to reopen."**: there's no lock to lift.
- **"The closing entry is already voucher No. … and December is closed, so it can't be changed."**: the closing is final and the year's balances changed since it was numbered. Reopen the months back to December (one at a time, starting from the last closed one), tap **Regenerate closing entry**, which keeps the number, and close again.
- **I need to fix a month from a while ago**: reopen month by month until you reach it or, better, record the adjustment in the current month with a manual voucher. See [Create, edit or reverse accounting vouchers](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/comprobantes-contables).
- **The balance says Not balanced**: review the month's manual vouchers with your accountant and generate the entries again. If it stays the same, contact support.

articles.title: Create, edit or reverse accounting vouchers
articles.summary: See every entry in the ledger, record a manual double-entry voucher and fix mistakes: edit or delete manual vouchers in an open month, or reverse a voucher once its month is closed.
articles.body:
Vouchers are your business's accounting entries: the ones MESAPAY builds from each month's operations and the ones you record by hand for adjustments, reclassifications or movements that don't go through the till. This is where you look them up, create them and fix them.

## Where to find them

Go to [Accounting › Vouchers](/operator/contabilidad/comprobantes). This section appears if your business has the accounting module; if you don't see it, contact support.

The list shows every voucher from the first of the month to today, with **Number**, **Date**, **Third party**, **Description**, **Source** and **Total**. To look at another period or find a specific voucher:

1. Type in **Search by number or description…** and set **From** and **To**.
2. Tap **Filter**. **Clear** takes you back to the current month.
3. Tap a voucher to see its lines, with the **Debits** and **Credits** totals and the **Balanced ✓** mark.

The **Source** tells you where the entry came from: **Manual** for the ones you record and, for the ones MESAPAY builds, names such as **Sales for the month**, **Expenses for the month**, **Payroll**, **Monthly depreciation** or **Bank movement**.

## When they get a number

While the month is open, vouchers show as **Unnumbered**. When you close the month, every voucher of that month (and any earlier one still without a number) gets its consecutive number in date order, for example #000123, and becomes final. See [Generate the entries and close the month](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/cerrar-el-mes-contable).

## Create a manual voucher

1. Tap **New voucher**.
2. Enter the **Date** and a **Description**, which is required; for example, "cash adjustment for a count difference".
3. If the movement involves someone, fill in **Third party (name)** and **Tax ID / document**, or tap **Pick** to search your suppliers and customers. The tax ID only accepts digits and hyphens, and it can't be entered without the name.
4. On each line, search for the account by **Account code or name** and enter the amount under **Debit** or **Credit**, never both. If you use cost centers, choose the **Center**. The line note is optional.
5. Tap **Add line** for any lines you still need. At least two are required.
6. Check **Total debits**, **Total credits** and **Difference** at the bottom. When it balances, **Balanced ✓** appears.
7. Tap **Save**.

You can only post in open months and to postable accounts, that is, accounts that accept movements (not header accounts).

> Manual vouchers are left untouched when MESAPAY regenerates the month's entries: they stay exactly as they are.

## Fix a voucher

What you can do depends on the source and on whether the month is open:

- **Manual, open month**: **Edit** or **Delete**. Deleting removes it from the ledger without a trace; if you'd rather keep a record, use **Reverse**.
- **Automatic, open month**: it isn't fixed by hand. Correct the source data (the expense, the purchase, the sale): the entry updates on its own the next morning, or right away if you tap **Generate / refresh entries** in [Accounting › Journal](/operator/contabilidad?tab=diario).
- **Any source, closed month**: only **Reverse**.

Reversing creates a new voucher with the same accounts and the debits and credits swapped, and marks the original as **Annulled**. Both stay in the ledger and offset each other. If the original's month is closed, the reversal is dated the first day of the first open month. Then record the correct entry with **New voucher**.

If a reversal isn't needed and its month is still open, delete it: the original goes back to **Posted**.

## Export

**Export CSV** downloads the voucher lines between **From** and **To**, with date, number, source, third party, tax ID, account, cost center, debit and credit, ready for your accountant.

## Common cases

- **"The entry does not balance: debits must equal credits."**: look at the **Difference** and correct the amounts.
- **"That month is closed. Reopen it from the Journal or post the entry in an open month."**: change the date to an open month or reopen the month, as explained in [Generate the entries and close the month](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/cerrar-el-mes-contable).
- **"the account does not accept movements (it is a header account)."**: choose a sub-account or create an auxiliary one, as explained in [Adjust the chart of accounts](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/plan-de-cuentas).
- **"Only manual vouchers can be edited or deleted; automatic ones are regenerated from the Journal."**: correct the source data and regenerate the month.
- **"A reversal cannot be reversed; if it is not needed, delete it."**: delete the reversal while its month is still open.
- **A bank movement or a deferral registration is wrong and there's no Edit or Reverse**: those entries aren't rebuilt when the month is generated. Offset them with a manual voucher with the accounts swapped, or reverse them once their month is closed.

articles.title: Reconcile your bank statement
articles.summary: Paste your bank statement in the Banks tab, post each movement to its account or let the rules do it, and ignore whatever MESAPAY already recorded another way.
articles.body:
Bank reconciliation brings into your books the bank movements that don't go through MESAPAY, such as bank fees, the 4x1000 tax or interest, while you review each line of the statement.

## Where to find it

In **Accounting › Expenses & journal**, **Banks** tab ([go to Banks](/operator/contabilidad?tab=bancos)). It requires the accounting module; if you don't see it, contact support.

## Import the statement

1. Download the statement from your online banking as CSV or Excel and copy the movement rows.
2. Paste them into **Import statement**: one line per movement, with date, description and amount.
3. Tap **Import**. The message tells you how many movements were imported and how many rows were skipped.

MESAPAY understands:

- Columns separated by semicolon, comma or tab.
- Dates like 15/10/2026 or 2026-10-15, in one of the first three columns.
- Amounts with periods or commas for thousands and decimals. A negative amount (with a minus sign or in parentheses) is money leaving the bank; a positive one, money coming in.

Rows without a date or an amount, such as headers, are skipped automatically.

> ⚠ MESAPAY takes the last number on each row as the amount. If your statement has a balance column, remove it before pasting; and if it has debits and credits in separate columns, merge them into one, with outflows as negatives.

> ⚠ Paste each statement only once: if you import the same period twice, the movements are duplicated. If that happens, mark the duplicates with **Ignore**.

## Post movement by movement

The pending movements appear below, with date, description and amount.

1. For each one, choose the account under **Account…**. The list shows postable income, expense and cost accounts.
2. Tap **Post**. An entry is recorded against bank account 111005 (Cuenta corriente / ahorros, current / savings account): money coming in is debited to the bank and credited to the chosen account; money going out, the other way round.
3. If the movement is already in your books some other way, tap **Ignore**.

Each posted movement becomes a voucher with source **Bank movement** in [Vouchers](/operator/contabilidad/comprobantes). They all go to that same bank account, even if you have several accounts at the bank.

> ⚠ Ignore whatever MESAPAY already posts for the month: sales, supplier payments and expense payments recorded in MESAPAY. If you also post them from the statement, they'll be counted twice.

## Automatic rules

For movements that repeat every month:

1. Under **Rules**, type some text in **If the description contains…** (for example, "4X1000" or "COMISION"), choose the **Account…** and tap **Add**.
2. Tap **Apply rules**. Every pending movement whose description contains that text is posted to the rule's account. Upper case and accents don't matter, and if several rules match, the one you created first wins.
3. To remove a rule, tap **Delete**.

Rules only run when you tap **Apply rules**, not when you import.

## Closed months

A movement dated in a closed month can't be posted. When you apply rules, those are skipped and the message tells you how many were in closed months. If it really has to be recorded in that month, reopen it first; see [Generate the entries and close the month](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/cerrar-el-mes-contable).

## Common cases

- **"That movement falls in a closed month — reopen the period first."**: reopen the month or, with your accountant, record the adjustment in the open month with a manual voucher.
- **Lots of skipped rows**: check that each line has the date in one of the first three columns and an amount other than zero.
- **I can't find the account in the list**: only postable income, expense and cost accounts appear. For a loan, a transfer between accounts or a payment to a third party, mark the movement with **Ignore** and record it with a [manual voucher](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/comprobantes-contables).
- **I posted a movement to the wrong account**: that entry can't be edited or deleted. Offset it with a manual voucher with the accounts swapped, or reverse it once the month is closed.

articles.title: Depreciate fixed assets and amortize deferrals
articles.summary: Record your equipment to depreciate it on a straight-line basis, and prepaid expenses or income received in advance to amortize them. MESAPAY posts each month's installment when you generate the entries.
articles.body:
Fixed assets and deferrals let you spread a large amount over several months: the depreciation of an oven or a fridge, or the amortization of an annual insurance policy paid upfront. You record the amount once and MESAPAY works out and posts each month's installment.

Both screens require the accounting module; if you don't see them, contact support.

## Fixed assets

They're in [Accounting › Fixed assets](/operator/contabilidad?tab=activos).

### Record an asset

1. Tap **New asset**.
2. Enter the **Name** and, if you like, a **Code** (the asset tag or an internal code).
3. Enter the **Purchase date**, the **Purchase value**, the **Salvage value** (what you expect it to be worth at the end of its useful life; it can be zero) and the **Useful life (months)**, which defaults to 60.
4. Choose the **Asset account**, an account in group 15; for example, 152405 Muebles y enseres (furniture and fixtures).
5. Check the **Accumulated depreciation account** (159205 by default) and the **Depreciation expense account** (516005 by default). Change them if your accountant uses others.
6. Tap **Save asset**.

### How it's calculated

- Straight line: (purchase value − salvage value) ÷ useful life = **Monthly quota**. The last installment adjusts the cents so the total adds up exactly.
- Depreciation starts the **month after** the purchase.
- Each month, MESAPAY builds a single **Monthly depreciation** entry with the installments of all assets: a debit to each one's expense account and a credit to its accumulated depreciation. It updates on its own every morning while the month is open, or when you tap **Generate / refresh entries** in [Accounting › Journal](/operator/contabilidad?tab=diario).

Tap an asset to see **Accumulated depreciation**, **Book value**, **First quota**, the **Posted depreciations** (each with **View entry**) and the **Remaining projection**.

### Edit or dispose

- **Edit** changes the data. Closed months aren't recalculated: the new base applies to open and future months.
- **Dispose** stops depreciation after the current month, which still gets its installment. **Reactivate** sets it back to **Active**.

> ⚠ This screen only posts depreciation. Record the purchase of the asset and its retirement (sale or write-off, with its book value) with a [manual voucher](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/comprobantes-contables), as your accountant tells you.

## Deferrals

They're in [Accounting › Deferrals](/operator/contabilidad/diferidos). You can also get there with the **Deferrals →** link on the assets tab.

### Record a deferral

1. Tap **New deferral**.
2. Enter a **Name** (for example, "annual insurance for the premises") and choose the **Type**: **Prepaid expense** or **Income received in advance**.
3. Enter the **Total amount**, the **Start date** and the number of **Months** to spread it over (1 to 120).
4. Choose the **Source account (cash / banks 11xx)**: where the money came from or went to.
5. Choose the bridge account: 17xx for a prepaid expense or 27xx for income received in advance.
6. Choose the target account: expense or cost (5xxx / 6xxx) or income (4xxx), depending on the type.
7. If you use cost centers, you can pick one. Add notes if you like and tap **Save deferral**.

When you save, two things happen:

- The **Initial entry** for the total is posted at once, on the start date. For an expense, debit to the bridge account and credit to cash or bank; for income, the other way round. Its source is **Deferral registration**.
- The first installment falls in the **same month** as the start date (unlike assets). Each installment goes into the **Deferral amortization** entry when you generate that month's entries.

### Tracking and write-off

Tap a deferral to see the **Monthly installment**, **Amortized to date**, **Balance to amortize** and the **Amortization schedule**, with each month marked **✓ Posted**, **Pending** or **Cancelled by write-off**.

**Write off** stops the amortization from the following month. Nothing is reversed: what's already amortized stays and the pending balance remains in the bridge account.

> ⚠ A deferral can't be edited or deleted. Check the amount, date, months and accounts before saving. If it's wrong, write it off and fix the balance with a manual voucher, with your accountant's help.

## Common cases

- **The month's installment doesn't show in the ledger**: generate the month's entries in **Accounting › Journal**; see [Understand how accounting works in MESAPAY](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/como-funciona-la-contabilidad).
- **"The asset account must be an active, postable 15 account."**: choose a group 15 account that accepts movements; if there isn't one, create it in [the chart of accounts](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/plan-de-cuentas).
- **"The salvage value must be lower than the purchase value."**: correct the salvage value.
- **"The start month is already closed."**: a deferral can't start in a closed month; use a date in an open month.
- **"No postable accounts with that prefix. Create them in the chart of accounts."**: create the missing account (for example, an auxiliary under 1705) and come back to the form.

articles.title: Build budgets and use cost centers
articles.summary: Set how much you expect to spend or sell per account in the chart of accounts each month, overall or per cost center, and compare it with the actuals in the ledger. Create and deactivate centers such as kitchen, bar or dining room.
articles.body:
A budget sets how much you expect to move in an account or group of the chart of accounts each month, and shows you how much you've actually moved. Cost centers (kitchen, bar, dining room, events…) let you split spending by area.

It's in [Accounting › Budgets](/operator/contabilidad?tab=presupuesto) and requires the accounting module; if you don't see it, contact support. Choose the month at the top with the ◀ ▶ arrows.

## Create cost centers

1. Scroll down to **Cost centers**.
2. Type the name in the center field (for example, Kitchen) and tap **Add**.
3. To stop using a center, tap **Deactivate**. It isn't deleted: its earlier movements are kept, and **Activate** makes it available again.

Active centers can be chosen when you record an expense, on each line of a [manual voucher](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/comprobantes-contables) and on a deferral.

## Add a budget

1. Under **Add budget**, search for the **Account** by code or name. You can choose an account that accepts movements or a two-digit group: a budget on 51 covers everything starting with 51.
2. Under **Cost center**, leave **General** or choose a center.
3. Enter the **Amount for the month**.
4. If it's the same amount all year, check **Apply to every month of the year**.
5. Tap **Save budget**.

If that account (with that center) already had a budget for the month, the amount is updated. If there's a **Whole year** budget and another one for a single month, the monthly one wins in that month.

## Read the execution

The month's execution table shows, per account and center:

- **Budget** and **Actual**. Actuals come from the month's ledger, which updates on its own every morning; to include today's activity, tap **Generate / refresh entries** in [Accounting › Journal](/operator/contabilidad?tab=diario).
- **Variance**: budget minus actual. On an expense account, a positive value means savings; a negative one means you went over.
- **% used**, with a traffic light: **on track** (up to 90%), **near limit** (up to 100%) and **over budget** (over 100%).

Actuals follow the nature of the account: for expenses and costs, debits minus credits; for income, credits minus debits. So you can budget sales too.

> A **General** budget adds up every movement in the account. A per-center budget only adds the ledger movements that carry that center: today, manual vouchers and deferral amortization. Expenses recorded with a center go into the month's entry without their center, so they don't show in the per-center execution yet.

## Delete a budget

Tap **Delete** on its row and confirm.

> ⚠ If the budget is a **Whole year** one, it's deleted for every month, even if you delete it while viewing a single month.

## Common cases

- **"No budgets for this month. Add the first one above."**: there are no budgets for the selected month yet; add one or check **Apply to every month of the year**.
- **Actual shows zero**: generate the month's entries; if the budget is per center, see the note above.
- **"That account is not in the chart (or is inactive)."**: activate it or choose another; see [Adjust the chart of accounts](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/plan-de-cuentas).
- **"That cost center does not exist or is inactive."**: activate it under **Cost centers** or choose another.
- **"An identical budget was saved at the same time. Reload and try again."**: reload the page and save again.

articles.title: Review your taxes and record their payment
articles.summary: Where to see the month's VAT or consumption tax and withholdings on purchases, how credit notes are subtracted, how to set up withholding concepts and the UVT, and how to record a tax payment.
articles.body:
MESAPAY uses what you sell and buy to calculate the period's VAT or consumption tax and the withholdings you applied, so your accountant can prepare the tax returns. These are reference figures: they don't replace the tax return or your accountant's review.

> The **Accounting** and **Reports** menus appear if your business has the accounting module. If you don't see them, contact support.

## Check the month's taxes

1. Go to [Accounting › Taxes](/operator/contabilidad?tab=impuestos) and pick the month with the arrows.
2. At the top you see the **Sales tax** your business invoices with. If it says **"This business is invoicing WITHOUT sales tax."**, tap **Configure** (see [Set up the sales tax](/operator/ayuda/facturacion/impuesto-de-ventas)).
3. Under **Taxes for the month** you see:

- With VAT: **VAT charged (sales)** minus **VAT deductible (purchases)** gives **VAT payable**. If the month had credit notes or refunds, instead of the first row you see **Gross VAT charged (sales)**, what was deducted (**VAT on credit notes**, **VAT on refunds without a credit note**) and **Net VAT charged**, and the deductible VAT is offset against the net.
- With consumption tax: **Consumption tax payable (sales)**, net of credit notes and refunds. If there were any, above it you see **Gross consumption tax charged (sales)** and what was deducted (**Consumption tax on credit notes**, **Consumption tax on refunds without a credit note**). VAT on purchases is not deducted from the consumption tax: it becomes part of the cost.
- **Withholdings applied on purchases**: **Income withholding**, **VAT withholding** and **ICA withholding** from the purchases received in the month.

Each invoice keeps the rate it was issued with: if the rate changed mid-month, each slice is added separately. The year-end closing is in this same tab (see [Generate the entries and close the month](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/cerrar-el-mes-contable)).

> **Taxes for the month** subtracts the credit notes accepted by the DIAN with an issue date in the month, at the rate of their lines, and gateway refunds without a credit note, at the month's rate. It's the same rule as **Period taxes**. If the net comes out negative (you refunded more than you sold), the amount payable stays at zero: review the credit balance with your accountant.

## See gross, credit notes and net

1. Go to [Reports › Period taxes](/operator/reportes/impuestos).
2. Choose **From** and **To** (or use **Previous month** / **Next month**) and tap **Apply**.
3. At the top, **Taxes generated**, **VAT generated** and **Consumption tax generated** are already sales minus refunds and credit notes.
4. In **Taxes generated on sales**, if there were refunds or credit notes, the columns **Gross tax**, **Refunds** and **Credit notes** appear; **Tax recorded** is the net amount.
5. Compare **Generated on sales** with **Recorded on purchases** and check the **Cross-check with the books**, which sets the documents against the ledger.

Only credit notes accepted by the DIAN are subtracted (a rejected or discarded one doesn't count), in the period of their issue date and at the rate of their lines. A payment gateway refund that already has a credit note is not subtracted twice. Sales count by the date the bill was paid.

What comes from the ledger (**Withholdings and other taxes from the ledger** and the cross-check) depends on the month's entries: until you generate them you'll see **"No movement in tax accounts in the period."** See [Understand how accounting works in MESAPAY](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/como-funciona-la-contabilidad).

To see it document by document, tap **Detailed taxes →**: each invoice (credit notes as negatives), each purchase and each withholding by voucher and third party, with **Export CSV** and **Print**.

## Set up withholding concepts and the UVT

In **Accounting › Taxes**, card **Withholdings (concepts)**, each concept shows its rate, its base (**on subtotal** or **on VAT**), its threshold in UVT and its account. Tap **Active** or **Inactive** to switch it: active concepts are suggested automatically when you record purchases. In **Current UVT value** type the year's value and tap **Save**. Your accountant decides which concepts apply.

## Record a tax payment

1. In **Accounting › Taxes**, pick the month of the period you paid.
2. In **Tax filings & payments**, choose the **Tax** (VAT (IVA), INC, Withholding or ICA) and enter the **Amount paid** and the **Payment date**.
3. Tap **Record payment for** followed by the month (for example, **Record payment for 2026-10**). You'll see **"Payment recorded and booked."**

The journal entry is created (tax account against bank) and the payment appears in the list.

## Common cases

- **"That tax already has a record for the period."**: that tax was already recorded for that month. A recorded payment can't be deleted from this screen: if you made a mistake, contact support.
- **"That movement falls in a closed month — reopen the period first."**: the payment date falls in a closed month. Reopen it first, as explained in [Generate the entries and close the month](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/cerrar-el-mes-contable).
- **There's a difference in the cross-check**: it doesn't prove an error. The ledger also includes payments, adjustments and [manual vouchers](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/comprobantes-contables); review them with your accountant.
- **"No documents with tax in the period."**: there were no paid invoiced bills or received purchases with tax on those dates.

articles.title: Prepare the exogenous information for the DIAN
articles.summary: Review formats 1001 to 1012 and 2276 for the tax year, fix third parties with issues, enter shareholders and investments, and download the official XML for the DIAN pre-validator.
articles.body:
Exogenous information (información exógena, also called medios magnéticos) is the yearly third-party report filed with the DIAN. MESAPAY builds each format from the year's purchases, expenses, invoices, receivables and payables, tax filings and payroll, so your accountant can validate it and upload it.

> It only applies to businesses registered in Colombia, and it's in the **Reports** menu, which appears with the accounting module.

## Open the tax year

1. Go to [Reports › Third-party information (exógena)](/operator/reportes/exogena).
2. In **Tax year** type the year you're reporting and tap **Apply**. If you don't choose one, it opens the previous year.
3. At the top you see the **UVT of the year**, the **Minor amount (1001)** and the **Minimum balance (1008/1009)**; below, the **Regulations for tax year**.

## Fix the issues

The **Issues** panel lists the third parties you need to fix before filing:

- **Blocks**: **No document number**, **The document has letters or symbols** or **No document type**. While it's there, that format's XML can't be downloaded.
- **Warning**: doesn't stop the download. For example, **The written check digit does not match the NIT (the XML carries the computed one)** or **No concept in the annex: shown but not exported to the XML**.

Tap **Fix** to go to the screen that holds the third party's data (**Suppliers**, **Customers**, **Invoices** or **Schedules**), correct it and come back to the report.

## What each format contains

Under **Computed from documents**:

- **1001**, payments or credits to account and withholdings applied: received purchases and expenses with a supplier, by third party and concept. An expense without a supplier doesn't appear here.
- **1005**, deductible VAT from received purchases, and under **VAT on returns** the VAT of your credit notes.
- **1006**, VAT generated and consumption tax by buyer. Sales without an invoice request go to **End consumer**.
- **1007**, income received (without tax or tip); under **Returns**, the base of your credit notes.
- **1008**, receivable balances at December 31 by customer: credit sales to your billing customers, minus refunds, payments and credit notes dated up to December 31, plus open credit voucher statements. A credit note issued in January doesn't lower the previous year's balance. You can compare it with [Receivables and payables](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/cartera) with **As of** set to December 31.
- **1009**, payable balances at December 31 from received purchases and expenses with a supplier.
- **1011**, the tax payments recorded in **Accounting › Taxes**. Only ICA goes into the XML.

Each credit note accepted by the DIAN uses the same third party as its invoice and subtracts what it returned. Under **Employment income (payroll)** you'll find **2276**, computed from settled payrolls; it shows **XML pending** because employees don't have a document number in MESAPAY.

## Enter shareholders and investments

Formats 1010 and 1012 don't come from documents: they go under **Manual entry**, for the selected year.

1. In **Register partner / shareholder** fill in **Name or company name**, **Document type**, **Number**, **Check digit**, **% ownership**, **Nominal value** and **Share premium**, and tap **Save**.
2. In **Register account / investment** choose the **Concept** (for example, savings accounts or term deposits), and fill in **Entity**, **Entity document type**, **Tax ID / document** and **Value at 12/31**. Tap **Save**.
3. To remove a record, tap **Delete** and confirm.

## Download the XML

Each format has its own **Download XML** button. The file comes out with the DIAN's official name, ready for its pre-validator. MESAPAY infers each third party's concepts, person type and location from its data: your accountant validates them in the pre-validator before filing.

### The 1001 TXT in the Taxes tab

In [Accounting › Taxes](/operator/contabilidad?tab=impuestos), the format 1001 card (for example, **Exógena 2026 (format 1001)**) summarizes payments to third parties for the year of the selected month and has **Download 1001 TXT**. Third parties without a valid NIT are left out of that file. It's a working summary: to upload to the DIAN, use the XML from the exogenous information report.

## Common cases

- **Download XML is disabled and says "Fix the issues to download"**: that format has blocking issues. Solve them with **Fix**.
- **"The document number must be numeric."** or **"The check digit does not match the NIT."**: in the manual entry, type only digits in the document (the check digit has its own field) and make sure it matches the NIT.
- **"No movements in the year."**: there are no documents for that format in the selected tax year. Check the year.
- **"Exogenous information is a DIAN (Colombia) regime…"**: your business is registered in another country, so this report doesn't apply.

articles.title: View the official books and financial statements
articles.summary: General journal, general ledger, trial balance, income statement and statement of financial position: how to filter them, check that they balance, drill down from a figure, export them to CSV and print them with page numbers.
articles.body:
The official books and financial statements show your business's accounting exactly as it was recorded in the vouchers. Use them to review balances, reconcile the period with your accountant and hand over the books as CSV or on paper.

## Before you start

- They live in the **Accounting** and **Reports** menus, which appear if your business has the accounting module. If you don't see them, contact support.
- They only show what is already in the books: the entries MESAPAY builds from each month's activity and the manual vouchers. Those entries update on their own every day at 5:30 a.m.; if sales, purchases or expenses came in today and you need them now, tap **Generate / refresh entries** on the **Journal** tab of **Accounting › Expenses & journal**, as explained in [Understand how accounting works in MESAPAY](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/como-funciona-la-contabilidad).
- The summary entries MESAPAY builds each month are dated the last day of the month. While the month is open, vouchers show as **unnumbered**: they are numbered when you [close the month](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/cerrar-el-mes-contable).

## How the filters work

1. Open them from the menu or from [Reports › All reports](/operator/reportes), under **Accounting** and **Financial**.
2. Enter the dates in **From** and **To**, or use the arrows to jump to the previous or next month (on the income statement, by year). The statement of financial position only asks for the **Cutoff date**.
3. Tap **Apply**.
4. **Export CSV** downloads the report with the same filters. **Print** opens the browser's dialog: each sheet carries the legal name, the tax ID (NIT), the name of the book, the period and its page number ("Page 1 of 3"; Google Chrome prints the page number). Collapsed rows are printed too.

> The filters stay in the page address: if you share the link with someone who has access to the dashboard, they see the same report.

## General journal

Under **Accounting › General journal / auxiliary** you see the period's vouchers in chronological order; it opens on the current month. Under **Journal mode**:

- **Itemized**: each voucher with its number, its source (for example **Sales for the month** or **Credit notes for the month**), the date and its **Debit** and **Credit** lines.
- **Summarized**: movements grouped by day and account, with the **Day total**.

At the top you see the **Vouchers**, **Total debits**, **Total credits** and the **Voided** ones, if any. A voided voucher is not deleted: it is marked **Voided** and its reversal appears separately, so they offset each other. The **Check** says **Double entry ✓** when debits and credits are equal.

## General ledger

Under **Accounting › General ledger** you see every account with movements or a balance, with its **Debit**, **Credit** and **Balance** for the period; it opens from January 1 to today.

1. Tap an account to see its **Opening balance for the period** and each movement with date, voucher, description and running **Balance**. **Expand all** opens them all.
2. To see a single account, type its code or name in **Account** and tap **Apply**. **Clear** removes the filter.

The balance follows the account's nature: debits minus credits for debit-nature accounts, credits minus debits for credit-nature accounts.

## Trial balance

Under **Reports › Trial balance** you see, per account, the **Opening balance** (everything before **From**), the **Debits**, the **Credits** and the **Closing balance**.

1. Under **Chart level**, choose **Class**, **Group**, **Account** or **Sub-account** (the default). Each level is the exact sum of what sits below it.
2. For a range of accounts, use **Account from** and **Account to**: `1105` to `1110` brings cash and banks, and the total becomes **Totals of the applied filter**.
3. Tap a class or group to expand it, or use **Expand all**.

Balances are signed, debit minus credit: credit balances (liabilities, equity, revenue) show as negative. The balance check always measures the whole book, even when you filter.

## Income statement

Under **Reports › Income statement** you see the period's revenue, costs and expenses; it opens from January 1 to today. Under **Fiscal year** you pick a full year, or leave **Custom range** and use the dates.

- At the top: **Revenue**, **Result for the period** and **Comprehensive income**.
- The charts **From revenue to result** and **Monthly trend**.
- The cascade with expenses by nature, from **Revenue from ordinary activities** to **Result before taxes**, **Income tax expense**, **Result for the period** and **Other comprehensive income**.
- The **Monthly summary**; a month cut by the range is marked **partial**.

The year-end closing entry is left out, so a closed year still shows its result. Credit notes accepted by the DIAN reduce revenue as sales returns (the **Credit notes for the month** entry). Outside Colombia, the statement is built by account type and the top shows **Result / revenue**.

> This statement comes from the accounting books. The **P&L** in Accounting is built directly from operations for day-to-day use: see [Read the monthly P&L and export the books](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/pyg-y-libros-del-mes).

## Statement of financial position

Under **Reports › Statement of financial position** you see **Assets**, **Liabilities** and **Equity** accumulated from the start of operations up to the **Cutoff date** (included; it opens with today).

- At the top, **Total assets**, **Total liabilities** and **Total equity**; at the bottom, **Total liabilities + equity**.
- The **Profit for the period** line in equity is the result of the open year, from January 1 after the last year-end closing. The profit of closed years is already in equity, in accounts 3605 and 3610.
- The **Check** says **Balanced ✓** when assets equal liabilities plus equity.

## From a figure to its detail

On both statements, every row with a code is a link: an account that takes postings opens its **General ledger**, and a group or parent account opens the **Trial balance** filtered by that code, for the same period.

For a quick look at a single month, the **Statements** tab of **Accounting › Expenses & journal** shows the **Trial balance**, the **Income statement** and the **Statement of financial position** with that month's entries.

## Common issues

- **"No movements in the period."**: there are no entries for those dates. Check the period and, if there was activity, generate the month's entries.
- **Today's sales or expenses are missing**: they come in with the next morning's update; to see them now, tap **Generate / refresh entries** and reload the report.
- **The vouchers say "unnumbered"**: the month is still open; they are numbered when it is closed.
- **"Out of balance by…"** or **"Double entry broken by…"**: write down the period and the difference and contact support.
- **"There are result accounts outside the usual prefixes…"**: there are revenue, cost or expense accounts with codes outside the chart (PUC). Review them in [Adjust the chart of accounts](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/plan-de-cuentas).
- **"Charts are not available because the amounts do not reconcile…"**: the table is still valid; contact support with the period.
- **It doesn't match the P&L**: they are different reports. The books also include manual vouchers, depreciation and deferrals.
