articles.title: Review your receivables and payables
articles.summary: Check, as of a cutoff date, how much your customers owe you and how much you owe your suppliers, with the age of each balance, each third party's statement and where to record payments.
articles.body:
Receivables and payables shows, as of a cutoff date, how much your customers owe you (accounts receivable) and how much you owe your suppliers (accounts payable), by third party and with the age of each balance.

> It's in the **Reports** menu, which appears with the accounting module. If you don't see it, contact support.

## What goes into it

- **Receivable (A/R)**: bills charged on credit to billing customers with credit enabled, and corporate voucher statements on credit, if you have the vouchers module. Since MESAPAY collects sales on the spot, other sales don't create receivables.
- **Payable (A/P)**: received purchase orders (for what was received) and non-recurring expenses that weren't recorded as paid.

When the DIAN accepts a credit note on a bill charged on credit, the customer's debt goes down by what the note cancels. The same happens with a refund. See [Issue an electronic credit note](/operator/ayuda/facturacion/notas-credito).

## Check your receivables and payables

1. Go to [Reports › Receivables & payables](/operator/reportes/cartera).
2. Choose **All**, **Receivable (A/R)** or **Payable (A/P)**.
3. In **As of** set the date and tap **Apply**. Only documents dated up to that day and payments made up to that day count: this lets you see the month-end position even if payments have come in since.
4. At the top you see **Total receivable** and **Total payable**, with how many customers, suppliers and documents there are.
5. In **Accounts receivable (by customer)** and **Accounts payable (by supplier)** you see each **Partner** with its **Tax ID**, **Documents**, **Oldest due date**, **Aging** and **Balance**.
6. Tap **Export CSV** to take it to a spreadsheet, or **Print**.

### How aging is measured

The **Aging** column counts from the due date: **Current**, **1–30 days**, **31–60 days** or **Over 60 days**. The due date is the one agreed on the document or, if it has none, the document date plus the terms:

- For a customer: **Terms (days)** in their billing customer record.
- For a supplier: **Payment terms (days)**.
- An expense is due on the date you set when you recorded it.

## See a third party's statement

1. Tap the customer's or supplier's name.
2. You'll see **Statement ·** and their name: documents and payments in order, with **Charge**, **Payment** and running **Balance**, and at the end **Total charges**, **Total payments** and **Closing balance**.
3. In **Outstanding balance by document age** the balance is split into **0–30 days**, **31–60 days**, **61–90 days** and **Over 90**, counting from the document date. **Total overdue** is what is past its due date.
4. Each document has a shortcut: **Open in purchases**, **Open in accounting**, **Open voucher statements** or **Open in customers**.
5. Tap **Print** to send the statement to the third party, or **Back to receivables & payables**.

## Where payments are recorded

This report only shows balances: payments are recorded where the debt started.

- **Customer with credit**: in [Orders › Customers](/operator/clientes), tap **Record payment** on the customer, fill in **Amount**, **Date**, **Account the money went into** and, if you like, **Note (optional)**, then tap **Record payment** in the form. The payment is applied to the oldest charge. See [Create customers to invoice](/operator/ayuda/facturacion/clientes-de-facturacion).
- **Supplier**: in [Purchasing](/operator/compras), open the purchase order and use **Register payment** or **Pay balance**, choosing in **Paid from** the account the money came from.
- **Expense**: if you check **Already paid** when you create it, it doesn't go into payables.

## Common cases

- **"No accounts receivable"** with a notice that the business has neither the vouchers module nor customers with credit: that's normal if everything is collected on the spot. To sell on credit, turn on **Allow paying on credit** for the customer.
- **A supplier shows as "No supplier"**: these are expenses recorded without a supplier. Edit the expense and assign the supplier.
- **The balance at a past date doesn't match today's**: that's expected if payments came in after the cutoff. Refunds and credit notes, however, are deducted at today's value.
- **"The payment cannot exceed the debt"**: enter an amount equal to or less than what the customer owes.

articles.title: Analyze your sales
articles.summary: See how much, when and what you sold in a period, compared with another: net sales, indicators, trend, day and hour, products and margin, team and payments. Tap any figure to filter and export to Excel or CSV.
articles.body:
Sales analysis shows how you sold in a period (how much, when, which dishes, who sold and how customers paid) compared with another period. Everything can be tapped: a bar, a cell or a name filters the whole analysis.

## Where it is and who sees it

Go to [Business › Sales analysis](/operator/reports/ventas). You also get there with **View analysis**, next to the last 7 days of sales on the **Summary**; with **Analyze this day**, on the **Close-out** screen; and, if you have the accounting module, from **Reports › All reports**, under **Commercial**.

Users with the Operator role can see it; waiters can't. It doesn't depend on any module.

## What net sales means

- **Net sales**: what was collected minus tips and taxes, with discounts already subtracted and without comps. It's the same figure as on the Summary.
- **Gross sales**: the dishes at menu price, tax included, before discounts.
- Tips aren't the business's sales. Comps, credit notes and refunds are shown separately.
- Each sale counts on the **business day** of its payment. By default the day runs from 5:00 to 5:00 the next day, Colombia time: what you collect after midnight counts for the night before. You can change the hour as explained in [Set your team's permissions, tips and shifts](/operator/ayuda/primeros-pasos/permisos-propinas-y-turnos).

At the bottom of the screen, **How is each figure calculated?** explains every number.

## Choose the period and the comparison

1. In **Period**, pick one, such as **Today**, **Yesterday** or **Last 30 days** (the one that opens by default), or **Custom range…** with **From**, **To** and **Apply**. A range can cover up to two years.
2. In **Compare with**, pick **Previous period**, **Same period last year** or **No comparison**.
3. In **Group by**, pick **Hour**, **Day**, **Week** or **Month**. Only the ones that make sense for the length of the period appear.

## Filter

Tap **More filters** and choose a channel (**Dining room**, **Counter**, **Takeout** or **Manual invoice**), waiter, category, product, payment method, table, day or hour. Each filter shows up as a tag at the top: tap it to remove it, or tap **Remove all filters**.

> With a product or category filter, the money figures are only for those lines. Tips, commissions, credit notes and refunds don't apply, because they belong to the whole check.

## Read the indicators

At the top are **Sales** (**Net sales**, **Gross sales**, **Taxes**, **Tips**, **Discounts and comps**, **Credit notes and refunds**) and **Checks and diners** (**Checks**, **Diners**, **Average check**, **Average per diner**, **Items per check** and **Table time**). Each one has an arrow against the compared period: green is better and red is worse. For discounts and returns, going up is worse.

## The charts

- **Trend**: net sales, checks or the average check (in **What to measure**), with the comparison overlaid.
- **Day and hour**: the heat map of the week, for periods of 7 days or more. It tells you the strongest day and hour.
- **Payments and channels**: what was collected by payment method (with tips), by channel, and the tables that sell the most.
- **Products and categories**: net sales, units, share and change for each product (sort them with **Top sales**, **Top units**, **Lowest sales** or **Lowest units**), the categories, the **Most ordered modifiers** and the available products that didn't sell.
- **Team**: each waiter's sales and commission, the one sealed when the check was paid. See [Settle your waiters' sales commissions](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/reporte-de-comisiones).

In **Trend** and **Day and hour**, **View as table** shows the numbers.

## Margin and menu engineering

If your business has the recipes module, **Menu engineering** places each dish by popularity and by unit margin (actual net price minus the cost of its recipe) in four groups: **Star**, **Plowhorse**, **Puzzle** and **Dog**, each with what to do. There, and in the products' **Unit margin** column, only dishes with a reliable cost count: with a recipe and all its ingredients costed. You need at least 3. If there aren't enough, you'll see **Not enough reliable cost yet** with the reason and the **Complete recipes and costs** button. The cost is each recipe's current cost.

## Drill down

1. Tap a bar, a cell, a point or a name: the whole analysis filters to it. In the daily trend, tapping a day takes you to that day.
2. The path you followed appears at the top. Tap a step to go back to it.
3. When the period is a single day, **Checks of the day** appears at the bottom, from newest to oldest. Tap one to open its detail. The first 500 are shown; to see them all, export.

## Export

**Export to Excel** and **Export CSV** download the current view, with its filters: the summary with the comparison, the trend, products, categories, modifiers, team, payments, channels, tables, day and hour and, for a single day, the checks. In Excel each part goes on its own sheet.

## Common cases

- **"No sales with these filters in the period."**: widen the period or tap **Remove all filters**.
- **It doesn't match the P&L**: the P&L adds up sales at menu price, with tax; net sales are without taxes or tips and with discounts subtracted. See [Read the monthly P&L and export the books](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/pyg-y-libros-del-mes).
- **Table time says "Not enough dining-room data"**: it's only shown if at least 60% of the period's dining-room checks can be measured.
- **"This screen is only for the restaurant's management."**: sign in with an Operator user.
- **I don't see Menu engineering**: it depends on the recipes module. Write to support if you need it.

articles.title: Settle your waiters' sales commissions
articles.summary: See how much each waiter collected in the period and their commission, with the percentage fixed on each bill when it was charged, review the bill-by-bill detail and download the CSVs to pay it.
articles.body:
The commissions report calculates, for a period, how much each waiter collected and how much commission they earned, so you can pay it or pass it on to payroll.

> It's in the **Reports** menu, which appears with the accounting module. If you don't see it, contact support.

## Before you start

Each waiter's percentage is set in **Settings › Tables by waiter**, under **Commission (%)**. See [Assign tables to each waiter](/operator/ayuda/primeros-pasos/mesas-por-mesero). A waiter with no percentage earns no commission.

## Check the report

1. Go to [Reports › Sales commissions](/operator/reportes/comisiones). It opens on the current month.
2. Choose **From** and **To** (or use **Previous month** / **Next month**) and tap **Apply**. The cutoff is by each bill's payment date.
3. At the top you see **Collected in the period**, **Commission to pay** and **People with commission**.
4. In **Summary by person** you see, for each waiter, **Bills**, **Collected**, **%** and **Commission**. If they had different percentages in the period, the **%** says **various**.
5. In **Bill-by-bill detail** you see each bill with its **Payment date**, the **Table** (or **Pickup** or **Manual invoice**), the person, the amount collected, the percentage and the commission.
6. Download **Summary CSV** or **Detail CSV** for your accountant, or tap **Print** to print the settlement.

## How it's calculated

- **The base** is the bill's collected subtotal, minus the diner's discount, without the tip and without tax: the consumption tax or VAT included in the price of the menu dishes is subtracted, and the tax added separately to a charge that isn't on the menu doesn't count either. A bill already charged keeps the base it was fixed with: if it was charged when the base still included the menu tax, it stays that way.
- **The commission is fixed when the bill is charged**: the waiter, their percentage, the base and the amount. If you change the percentage, it only affects bills charged afterwards.
- **Only paid bills count.** An open bill earns no commission, and neither do complimentary or zero-value bills.
- **The bill's waiter** is the one who charged it. If several waiters charged it, the one who collected the most gets it. If no waiter charged it (the diner paid from the QR or it was charged at the register), it goes to the waiter assigned to that table, as long as there is only one. If there is none, the bill earns no commission.

> ⚠ Refunds made after the payment are not deducted from the commission automatically: subtract them yourself when you pay it.

This report only calculates: it doesn't create journal entries or payroll payments.

## What the waiter sees

In their app, in the **Yo** (Me) tab, the waiter sees **My commissions**: **This month** or **Last month**, with their **Commission**, the amount **Collected**, the **Bills**, **Your %** and the **Latest bills**. It appears if they have a percentage set or already have bills with commission that month.

> Each waiter's sales and commission also appear in the **Team** panel of the sales analysis, with filters and comparison. See [Analyze your sales](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/analizar-las-ventas).

## Common cases

- **"No bills with commission in the period."**: the waiter had no percentage when the bills were charged, or the bills weren't attributed to them. Check their **Commission (%)** in [Tables by waiter](/operator/settings/meseros); bills already charged are not recalculated.
- **A waiter is missing bills the diner paid from the QR**: those bills go to the waiter assigned to the table. If nobody had the table, or two waiters had it, they earn no commission. Assign each table to a single waiter.
- **The % says "various"**: the percentage changed within the period. Check the **Bill-by-bill detail**.
- **A refund was made on a bill already settled**: deduct that part of the commission manually when you pay.

articles.title: Ask Pulso about your business
articles.summary: Pulso is the AI assistant that answers questions about your sales, dishes, waiters, tables, kitchen and reservations using your business's real data. It comes with the Pro plan and the trial, with a daily question limit.
articles.body:
Pulso is an AI assistant that answers questions about how your restaurant is doing: what sells, when it gets busiest, how your waiters perform or at what times the kitchen falls behind. You'll find it in the **Business › Pulso** menu.

## Ask a question

1. Go to [Business › Pulso](/operator/insights).
2. Tap a suggested question, such as **What are my best-selling dishes this month?**, or type your own and tap **Send**.
3. While it looks up the data you see **Analyzing your data…**. The answer brings the key figures, comparisons and one or two recommendations, in the language your dashboard is set to.
4. Keep asking in the same conversation ("and last month?"). If you leave the screen or reload it, a new conversation starts.

> Say the period in your question: "this week", "in September", "Saturdays over the last three months". If you don't, it usually looks at the last 30 days.

## What data it uses

Pulso looks up your business's data at the moment you ask and does not make up figures: if something can't be answered with that data, it tells you. It knows about:

- Sales: revenue, orders, average ticket, guests and their trend versus the previous period.
- Dishes and categories: best and worst sellers, by quantity or by revenue.
- Payments: how much comes in through each payment method and how much in tips.
- Waiters: sales, payments, tables and tips based on who took the payment (what guests pay on their own from the QR is not assigned to anyone), and how many waiters you need per time slot.
- Floor and kitchen: table turnover, peak hours and when preparation takes longer than each station's target time.
- Cancellations and comps, what guests search for on the menu, and reservations with their no-shows and deposits.

It does not look at accounting, expenses, purchases, inventory, payroll or electronic invoices: the [accounting reports](/operator/ayuda/contabilidad-y-reportes/libros-y-estados-financieros) cover those.

## Which plans include it and how many questions you get

- It comes with the Pro plan and during the trial period. The basic plan doesn't include it, unless MESAPAY turns it on for your business.
- There is a daily question limit for the whole business, adding up every dashboard user's questions: 50 a day by default. The day runs from midnight to midnight in your business's time zone (in Colombia, Bogotá time). A question that couldn't be answered doesn't count.

## Common issues

- **"The Pulso assistant is not enabled for this business."**: your plan doesn't include it. Contact support if you want to turn it on.
- **"You've reached today's question limit."**: the day's questions are used up. Continue the next day, or contact support if your team needs more.
- **"Something went wrong. Please try again."**: send the question again; that one wasn't counted.
- **The figure doesn't match an accounting report**: check that the period is the same. Pulso works with floor operations (orders and payments), not with the accounting books.
